ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the point $P(-4, 3)$ is on the graph of the linear function $y = kx + b$ (where $k \neq 0$). Then, what is the solution set of the inequality $kx + b < 3$ with respect to $x$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} When $x > -4$, $y < 3$, i.e., $kx + b < 3$,\\
thus the solution set of the inequality $kx + b < 3$ with respect to $x$ is $x > -4$.\\
Therefore, the answer is: $\boxed{x > -4}$.

Then reason: To solve kx+b<3 is to find the range of x for which the function value y on the graph is less than 3.
